key_insight: Noise-informed error correction can keep logical memory and logic high-performing on a heterogeneous 156-qubit heavy-hex superconducting processor by adapting schedules, decoding, and post-selection to imperfect hardware.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how practical quantum processors can tolerate fabrication variability while still supporting fault-tolerant memory and logical operations, which is important for scaling superconducting quantum computers.
method: Dynamic compass code on a 156-qubit heavy-hex lattice
Exclude underperforming qubits/couplers via redesigned measurement schedules
Use noise-informed decoding and leakage-aware post-selection
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 35% lower logical memory error, up to 56% improvement in measurement-based logic, and Bell fidelities rising from above 77% to above 97% with layered filtering and decoding.
watch_item: The gains rely on careful hardware-specific calibration, qubit/coupler exclusion, and post-selection, which may reduce usable data rate and may not transfer directly across processors without retuning.
paper_title: Error-Corrected Memory and Logic on a Heavy-Hex Superconducting-Qubit Processor
